headline.purpose: Every page's single <h1> title. Top-left, never centered.

title.purpose: Dialog titles (bold, 18px); card titles use a quieter semibold 16px step.

body.purpose: Default UI text — table cells, form fields, descriptions.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracking-wide section captions and metadata. Never used for clickable text.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: The system's only shadow — dialogs, popovers, dropdown menus, date-picker calendar. Never applied to at-rest surfaces.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default easing for color/background/border transitions (hover, focus, active-state changes).

motion.name: press-feedback
motion.purpose: 1px downward translate on :active for every button variant — the system's one piece of tactile motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Pill-shaped, System-Blue button with hover-invert and a sliding directional arrow — the default call-to-action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; font-family: var(--font-sans, sans-serif); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.2s, color 0.2s, transform 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--foreground); color: var(--background); } .ds-btn-primary:hover .ds-btn-arrow-line { background: var(--background); } .ds-btn-primary:hover .ds-btn-arrow-line::after { right: 0; border-color: var(--background); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--ring); } .ds-btn-arrow { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; } .ds-btn-arrow-line { position: relative; display: block; width: 10px; height: 2px; background: var(--primary-foreground); transition: background-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-arrow-line::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: -3px; right: 3px; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-right: 2px solid var(--primary-foreground); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--primary-foreground); transform: rotate(-45deg); transition: right 0.2s, border-color 0.2s; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Transparent, hairline-bordered text input with a System-Blue focus ring.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Search by name or role…" />
components.css: .ds-input { height: 32px; width: 100%; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-lg); background: transparent; color: var(--foreground); font-size: 0.875rem; font-family: var(--font-sans, sans-serif); outline: none; transition: border-color 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-input:focus { border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat, ring-bordered surface — one lightness step brighter than the page background, no shadow at rest.
components.html:
Priya Patel
12 assigned profiles
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--card); border-radius: var(--radius-xl); padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 10%, transparent); font-family: var(--font-sans, sans-serif); } .ds-card-title { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--foreground); } .ds-card-desc { margin-top: 4px; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--muted-foreground); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Pill badge in the muted per-status color family (shown here as Applied). The intended coloring for application status — the current build renders these with the flat neutral secondary variant instead.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 20px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; font-family: var(--font-sans, sans-serif); } .ds-badge-applied { background: var(--status-applied); color: var(--status-applied-foreground); }

components.name: Initials Avatar
components.description: Circular initials badge in one of six muted hues, deterministically hashed per person name. The system's signature identity component.
components.css: .ds-avatar { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 24px; height: 24px; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 0.65rem; font-weight: 500; font-family: var(--font-sans, sans-serif); } .ds-avatar-blue { background: var(--avatar-1); color: var(--avatar-1-foreground); }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Icon+label navigation row; active state is an Accent Wash fill, never an underline or border.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: var(--radius-md); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; font-family: var(--font-sans, sans-serif); color: var(--muted-foreground); text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--muted); color: var(--foreground); } .ds-nav-item-active { background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-foreground); }

narrative.overview: This is Nova Staffs' internal recruiting operations tool, not a marketing surface — recruiters and admins live in it all day, so the design's job is to disappear and let the work show through. One restrained accent (System Blue) carries every signal of action and focus; everything else stays neutral, flat, and quiet. Status and identity are color-coded, but deliberately desaturated, so the eye reads structure and activity, never noise. The aesthetic is calm, precise, and unshowy — closer to an iOS system app than a dashboard product. Surfaces stay flat at rest, corners are generously and consistently rounded, and typography leans on scale and weight contrast rather than color to establish hierarchy. It explicitly rejects the generic dense enterprise-SaaS look: no heavy gray chrome, no cramped zebra tables, no shouting for attention. Interaction feedback (hover inversion, a sliding directional arrow, a 1px press) gives the restraint a pulse instead of making it feel inert.
keyCharacteristics: Single accent color (System Blue), used sparingly and only for action/focus/active state
Flat surfaces (ring/border, not shadow) at rest; shadow reserved for content that floats above the page
Muted, desaturated semantic color families for status badges and person-avatars, never saturated brights
Generous, consistent corner rounding across buttons, cards, badges, and avatars
Tabular-numeral stat tiles and uppercase tracking-wide eyebrow labels for structure without added color or weight

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: System Blue is the only saturated color allowed anywhere in the interface. Every other color — status, avatar, semantic — is desaturated to roughly the same low-chroma recipe. If a new color is needed, it must fit that recipe, not introduce new saturation.

rules.name: The Tint-Never-Fill Rule
rules.body: Destructive and accent-wash colors are applied as low-opacity tints or /10–/20 backgrounds, never as solid saturated fills outside the primary button/badge.

rules.name: The Scale-Not-Color Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is built with size and weight jumps (14→16→18→30px, normal→medium→semibold→bold), not with color or a second typeface. A heavier or larger element always outranks a colored one.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Any numeral that represents a live count (applications, interviews, offers, stat tiles) renders with tabular-nums so digits don't shift width as they update.

rules.name: The Two-Rail Rule
rules.body: A page never has more than two left-hand rails at once: the primary app sidebar, and optionally one page-local Views/filter rail. If a page needs more filtering than that, it goes in the toolbar row (search, chips), not a third rail.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing that sits in the page's normal flow — card, table, sidebar, stat tile — ever gets a box-shadow. If it needs to be distinguished, use a ring/border and a background-lightness step, not depth.

dos: Do keep System Blue as the only saturated color in the interface — every other hue (status, avatar, semantic) stays in the same low-chroma, high-lightness recipe.
Do keep cards, tables, and any at-rest surface flat (ring/border only); reserve the single overlay shadow for dialogs, popovers, and dropdowns.
Do use tabular-nums on any numeral that represents a live, updating count.
Do use the uppercase, tracking-wide, muted-foreground eyebrow-label pattern for section/group headers instead of a heavier headline.
Do give primary (default variant) buttons the hover-invert + sliding-arrow treatment; keep every other button variant flat-colored with only the shared press/focus feedback.
Do cap forms and detail/review pages at max-w-3xl–max-w-5xl; leave list/table pages full-width.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated accent color. If something needs to stand out, use System Blue, weight, or size — not a new hue.

Don't add box-shadow to anything that sits in the page's normal flow (cards, tables, sidebars, stat tiles) — that reads as generic enterprise-SaaS clutter, the explicit anti-reference for this system.
Don't render a solid, fully-saturated fill for destructive or semantic colors — tint them, per the Tint-Never-Fill Rule.
Don't mix typefaces for hierarchy. One family (Google Sans) at every weight/size step; contrast comes from scale, not font-switching.
Don't add a max-w-* cap to a list/table page, or leave a form/detail page uncapped — both break the system's one layout-width convention.
